# Compare Chronobiome Serial Sampling Data to UKBB Olink Proteomics Data

Loads the serial-sampling Olink study and the baseline UKBB fits, and defines `getGamFitSerial()`, which fits a diurnal GAM to the serial data adjusted for age group and sex, with a random intercept for each subject.

```{r}
library(reshape2)
library(dplyr)
library(mgcv)
library(ggplot2)

# UKBB side, from ChronobiomeUKBB.Rmd: fitting functions, baseline model dataframe (section 4.1)
# and spline fits (section 7). X is loaded only if this session does not already have it.
source("ChronoFunctions.R")
if (!exists("X")) load("outputs/savedX.Rdata") # X and BIOMARKER_NAMES
OBSERVED <- readRDS("outputs/saveOBSERVED.Rds")

# Read subject data from 2025-09-17_Common-chronobiome-and-ukbb-cyclers_Sample-metadata_AB-proteomics_Plasma_NPX-values.txt
SAMPLE_INFO <- read.table("support_files/2025-09-17_Common-chronobiome-and-ukbb-cyclers_Sample-metadata_AB-proteomics_Plasma_NPX-values.txt", header = TRUE, sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# Read biomarker data from 2025-09-17_Common-chronobiome-and-ukbb-cyclers_Feature-matrix_AB-proteomics_Plasma_NPX-values.txt
SAMPLE_DATA <- read.table("support_files/2025-09-17_All-protein-assays_Feature-matrix_AB-proteomics_Plasma_NPX-values.txt", header = TRUE, sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
# Reshape data to long format for time-series analysis
SERIAL <- melt(SAMPLE_DATA, id.vars = c("Feature_id", "Symbol"), variable.name = "Sample_id", value.name = "value") %>% 
  left_join(SAMPLE_INFO, by = "Sample_id")
```

```{r}
# Function to fit Generalized Additive Model (GAM) to serial sampling data
# Adjusts for Age, Sex, and includes Subject_id as a random effect
getGamFitSerial <- function(biomarker, plotdata = FALSE, adjustforSex = TRUE) {

  tmpdf <- SERIAL %>%
    filter(Symbol == biomarker) %>%
    filter(!is.na(value)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(Sex)) %>%
    mutate(Subject_id = factor(Subject_id)) # bs = "re" needs a factor

  # tryCatch fit gam as function of Clock_time subject level as random effect Subject_id
  gamfit <- NULL

  tryCatch({
    # Model: Outcome ~ Smooth(Time) + Fixed(Age, Sex) + Random(Subject)
    # Age group and sex are constant within a subject, so they are only estimable with subject as a
    # random intercept. REML is the usual choice with random effects, and matches bam's fREML in getGamFit.
    gamfit <- mgcv::gam(value ~ s(Clock_time, k = 6) + Age_group + Sex + s(Subject_id, bs = "re"),
                        data = tmpdf, method = "REML")
  }, error = function(e) {
    print(paste("Error in gam fit for", biomarker, ":", e$message))
    return(NULL)
  })
  
  if (plotdata) {
    pout <- ggplot(tmpdf, aes(Clock_time, value)) + 
      geom_point() + 
      geom_smooth(method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, k = 6)) + 
      theme_bw(base_size = 16) + 
      ggtitle(biomarker) + xlab("Time of day (hours)") + ylab("NPX") + 
      theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
    
    print(pout)
  }
  return(gamfit)
}   
fit <- getGamFitSerial("SNCA", plotdata = TRUE)
as.vector(fit$coefficients[grepl("Clock_time", names(fit$coefficients))])

# fit gam models to SAMPLE_DATA
```

# Plotting functions comparison to UKBB

Functions that overlay the serial and UKBB diurnal curves of a protein (`compareFits`, `compareBiomarkerSet`) and correlate the two curves (`correlationSerialUKBB`); the UKBB curve comes from good-health participants, adjusted for sex. The last chunk computes the correlation for every protein in the serial data.

```{r}
greatHealth <- X$health_rating == "Excellent" | X$health_rating == "Good"

# Compare the fitted curve from local Serial data with UKBB reference data
compareFits <- function(biomarker) { 
    fitSerial <- getGamFitSerial(biomarker, plotdata = FALSE)
    if (is.null(fitSerial)) { return(NA) }
    
    pdf(NULL)
    plotdata <- mgcv::plot.gam(fitSerial, select = 1)[[1]] # the Clock_time smooth, not the subject random effect
    plotdf <- data.frame(x = plotdata$x, fit = plotdata$fit, se = plotdata$se, dataset = "Serial")
    plotdf$x <- plotdf$x / 100 # convert to hours
    dev.off()

    tmpdf <- getGamFit(biomarker, adjustforSex = TRUE, rowsubset = greatHealth, plotdata = TRUE)
    tmpdf$dataset <- "UKBB"

  mycolors <- c("#E41A1C", "#377EB8")
  p0 <- ggplot(rbind(plotdf, tmpdf), aes(x, fit, color = dataset)) + 
    geom_line(size = 1) + 
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = fit - se, ymax = fit + se, fill = dataset), alpha = 0.2, color = NA) + # se from plot.gam is already 2 standard errors
    theme_bw(base_size = 16) + 
    ggtitle(biomarker) + xlab("Time of day (hours)") + ylab("NPX") + 
    scale_fill_manual(values = rev(mycolors)) +
    scale_color_manual(values = rev(mycolors)) +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
  return(p0)
}


correlationSerialUKBB <- function(biomarker) { 
    if (!biomarker %in% BIOMARKER_NAMES$biomarker) { return(data.frame()) }
  
    fitSerial <- getGamFitSerial(biomarker, plotdata = FALSE)
    if (is.null(fitSerial)) { return(data.frame()) }
    
    
    tmpdf <- getGamFit(biomarker, adjustforSex = TRUE, rowsubset = greatHealth, plotdata = TRUE)
    
    pdf(NULL)
    plotdata <- mgcv::plot.gam(fitSerial, select = 1, xlim = range(tmpdf$x * 100))[[1]]
    plotdf <- data.frame(x = plotdata$x, fit = plotdata$fit, se = plotdata$se, dataset = "Serial")
    plotdf$x <- plotdf$x / 100 # convert to hours
    dev.off()
    
    # significance of correlation between the two fitted curves
    cor.test.out <- cor.test(plotdf$fit, tmpdf$fit)
    tmp <- broom::tidy(cor.test.out)
    tmp$biomarker <- biomarker
    return(tmp)
}

compareBiomarkerSet <- function(biomarkers) { 
  
  MINIMAL_THEME<- theme_minimal() +
    theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 20, hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 14),
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(color = "grey85", linewidth =1),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "grey85", linewidth =0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),    # Remove intermediate grid lines
    #panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1)
  ) 

  PLOTS <- list()
  for (bm in biomarkers) {
    p0 <- compareFits(bm)
    p0 <- p0 + MINIMAL_THEME + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 20), breaks = c(0,4,8,12,16,18,20)) + 
      scale_y_continuous(
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.1, 0.2)),
      breaks = function(lims) sort(unique(c(pretty(lims), lims[2]))),
      labels = scales::label_number(accuracy = 0.1, drop0trailing = TRUE) #
    )
    PLOTS[[bm]] <- p0
  }
  return(PLOTS)
}
```

```{r}
# compute correlations for all symbols present in the serial data
CORRELATIONS <- bind_rows(lapply(unique(SERIAL$Symbol), correlationSerialUKBB))
```

# Plot Diurnal Pattern Correlation (UKBB and Chronobiome) by different cutoffs

Plots the mean serial-UKBB curve correlation as the UKBB oscillation threshold rises (`figures/ChronobiomeSerialCorrelationByCutoff.pdf`), and overlays the curves of strong and weak UKBB oscillators (`figures/ChronobiomeSerialHigh.pdf`, `figures/ChronobiomeSerialLow.pdf`).

```{r}
# Load external Chronobiome/UKBB cosinor fit results for comparison
OlinkChronobiome <- read.csv("support_files/Cosinor-lmer_Fit-across-all-samples_Olink_Plasma_Proteomics.txt", sep = "\t")

tmp <- OBSERVED %>% 
  left_join(BIOMARKER_NAMES) %>%  
  filter(population == "good_health_all" & type == "Protein") %>%
  left_join(OlinkChronobiome, by = c("biomarker" = "Assay")) %>%
  left_join(CORRELATIONS, by = "biomarker")

# Analyze how correlation between datasets changes as we filter for stronger cyclic signals in UKBB
CORRELATION_SUMMARY <- data.frame()

for (cutoff in seq(0, 6, by = 0.1)) { 
  z <- tmp %>% filter(log(statistic.x) > cutoff & !is.na(estimate))
  
  CORRELATION_SUMMARY <- rbind(CORRELATION_SUMMARY, 
                            data.frame(cutoff = cutoff, 
                                       mean = mean(z$estimate), 
                                       sd = sd(z$estimate), 
                                       n = nrow(z)))
}

pdf("figures/ChronobiomeSerialCorrelationByCutoff.pdf", width = 8, height = 6)
ggplot(CORRELATION_SUMMARY, aes(cutoff, mean)) + geom_line() + geom_point() + 
  theme_bw(base_size = 16) + 
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = mean - 2 * sd/sqrt(n), ymax = mean + 2 * sd/sqrt(n)), alpha = 0.2, fill = "lightblue") +
  xlab("UKBB log(statistic) Threshold") + 
  ylab("Average Correlation") +
  ggtitle("Correlation of Diurnal Patterns (UKBB vs Chronobiome)") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5))
dev.off()

```

```{r}
btype <- "Protein"
# Select top low-confidence and high-confidence cyclers based on p-value and statistic thresholds
CYCLERSLOW <- OBSERVED %>% left_join(BIOMARKER_NAMES) %>%  
    filter(population == "good_health_all" & type == btype & !grepl("percentage", biomarker)) %>% 
    filter(p.value > 0.01 & statistic < 6) %>% 
    arrange(range) %>%  head(51) 

CYCLERSHIGH <- OBSERVED %>% left_join(BIOMARKER_NAMES) %>%  
    filter(population == "good_health_all" & type == btype & !grepl("percentage", biomarker)) %>% 
    filter(p.value < 0.01 & statistic > 6) %>% 
    arrange(desc(range)) %>%  head(50) 


PLOTSLOW <- compareBiomarkerSet(head(CYCLERSLOW$biomarker,40))
pdf("figures/ChronobiomeSerialLow.pdf", width = 11.5, height = 16)
ggpubr::ggarrange(plotlist = PLOTSLOW, ncol = 4, nrow = 10 )
dev.off()

PLOTSHIGH <- compareBiomarkerSet(head(CYCLERSHIGH$biomarker,40))
pdf("figures/ChronobiomeSerialHigh.pdf", width = 11.5, height = 16)
ggpubr::ggarrange(plotlist = PLOTSHIGH, ncol = 4, nrow = 10)
dev.off()
```
